expectations.text: The reply shows the saving net and by quarter, starting from realistic exit dates, rather than presenting 120 × €75,000 as the 2027 saving.
expectations.evidence: The 'Phasing' sheet runs month by month for 2027–28 under three timings; base case 'Netherlands… exits 31 May', 'Germany… exits 31 July'; reply table 'Full saving from (DE / NL) Aug / Jun', '2027 net cash −1.9'; the Checks sheet shows 'ALL OK'. Monthly rather than quarterly, which is finer.

expectations.text: The reply includes the delays from consultation, notice periods and notification duties in Germany and the Netherlands, flagged for counsel.
expectations.evidence: Germany: §§111–112 BetrVG; 'the mass-dismissal notification, which can only be filed once consultation is complete. The Federal Labour Court ruled on 1 April 2026 that filing it earlier makes the dismissals invalid' (verified, 6 AZR 152/22); §622 BGB. Netherlands: art. 25 WOR, WMCO, UWV permits or settlements, then notice. 'Have employment counsel in both countries confirm the timeline before anything is announced.'

expectations.text: The reply includes one-off costs (such as severance, transition payments or a social plan, and outplacement) and hidden costs (such as work still to be done, revenue at risk, rehiring and extra attrition), with estimates labelled.
expectations.evidence: One-offs: severance DE 1.0 and NL 0.5 months per year, transition support €6k, legal €0.5m (range €3.3–9.3m total). Hidden costs: 'Roles refilled or covered by agency or contractors 10%… at 1.2× cost', 'Extra voluntary turnover among the 1,280 who stay +1 point'; revenue at risk named in 'Not in the model… For the savings above to hold, this must be close to zero'. A Confidence column grades each input.

expectations.text: The reply says plainly whether the €9 million arrives in 2027, with arithmetic that adds up.
expectations.evidence: 'that plan saves about €4.5m gross in 2027 and is about €1.9m cash-negative in 2027'. Checked: 4.5 − 0.54 − 0.168 − 5.72 = −1.928; payback April 2028; run-rate 9.0 − 1.08 = 7.92.

expectations.text: The reply compares the redundancy plan with alternatives that cost fewer jobs, on the same basis, before recommending.
expectations.evidence: §5 'Options side by side' (do nothing, third-party spend, pricing, insourcing, stopping work, hiring freeze '~2.0 (illustrative)' / '~4.3' with '15% assumed' cover, redeployment, executive bonuses, Kurzarbeit, voluntary exits, compulsory 120 '−1.9 net cash' / '7.9') in the same columns, before §7 'Decisions requested'. Unsized levers are marked 'To size' with their data source.

expectations.text: The reply keeps the numbers honest: restructuring is not presented as one-off when it recurs, assumptions are stated, and it shows sensitivities or a break-even.
expectations.evidence: Sensitivity grid of timing × one-off level (+2.1 to −7.4); payback per scenario; an assumption table with 'Basis' and 'Confidence'; provision timing ('It moves the P&L charge between years; it doesn't change the cash'); no lever sized without a basis.

overall_quality.evidence: An honest, well-structured board paper and reconciled monthly model that asks the board to approve consultation rather than a number, owns responsibility, and sizes only what it can.

factual_errors.evidence: Verified: BAG 1 April 2026 (6 AZR 152/22, notification before consultation ends makes dismissals invalid), €102,000 cap for 2026, Wet personeelsbehoud bij crisis (36940) still before the Tweede Kamer, Kurzarbeit 12 months from 2027, art. 25(6) WOR.

skill_leak.evidence: No skill, reference-file or ladder jargon; 'From each seat' is plain English.

owns_result.evidence: The prompt states no bad outcome. The paper still says 'The gap this programme has to close is the result of management decisions, and management owns it.'

best_insight.value: Cites the Federal Labour Court's 1 April 2026 ruling that a notification filed before consultation ends voids the dismissals, showing why announcing a number first can't speed things up.

suggestions.reason: No assertion rewards framing the board decision correctly (approve consultation on the target, not the announcement of a headcount), which is the most useful thing this sample does for a finance director facing a CEO deadline.

eval_feedback.overall: Meets every assertion with substance; among the best.
